name: Odiham Castle (King John's Castle): the keep
about: The ruined octagonal keep of King John's castle (1207-14), standing alone in its clearing by the Basingstoke Canal. A scheduled monument. On its own map for now (Odiham_castle, turned as Odiham is), to join to Odiham's later.
evidence: Wikipedia (Odiham Castle, facts only): built 1207-14, 'a three-storey stone keep ... The only visible remains are part of the octagonal keep and outlying earthworks', at 51.26142 N 0.96172 W.
OSM: the keep's walls as a barrier=wall ring about 17 m across, centre (463, 442) on this map: the ruin stands on it and replaces it.
Photos (Commons, Category:Odiham Castle, looked at only): pale grey flint rubble, two to three storeys, ragged tops, broken low on one side, round-arched breaches, a round window, putlog holes.
